clue.text: Copper and friend nabbing fellow in the big match

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: to nab is to grab hold of, so the friend's word closes round the fellow and the in

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A police officer and a mate collar a man at the big football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal, Cu. The FA Cup Final is the showpiece match of the English football season.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup final is the deciding game of a knockout competition, the biggest match of the tournament.

clue.text: What despairing defence counsel wants to do? He has a trick or two

definitions.text: What despairing defence counsel wants to do?
definitions.meaning: a lawyer with a hopeless case might wish to trick a member of the jury

definitions.text: He has a trick or two

explanation.surface: A desperate barrister wants to fool the court, and a trickster is at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror is a stage magician, a performer whose act consists of sleight-of-hand tricks.

clue.text: Film franchise advertisement held up amidst dreadful report

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so one piece is set inside the other
dreadful signals that the letters of report are reworked badly
in a down entry, held up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A newspaper story says a movie series' promotion was delayed by a terrible report.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'held up' reads the letters bottom to top; 'dreadful' scrambles the report into PRETOR, which 'amidst' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: Predator is the sci-fi action movie series begun in 1987 with Arnold Schwarzenegger hunted by an alien.

clue.text: Murdoch, perhaps, is fairish? Not entirely

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the word fairish, its outer letters left off

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person named Murdoch is fair-haired, and answers not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch was the Anglo-Irish novelist of The Sea, the Sea, so she is one example of a person with this first name.

clue.text: Oratorio that's peculiar — I claim — for the duo

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, signalling these letters are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A singer claims an oratorio is odd and suits a pair of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Child of Our Time is Michael Tippett's 1940s oratorio, a large choral work, reacting to Nazi persecution.

clue.text: Russian river passing through Ukraine vaguely

indicators.note: the answer runs through the two words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A Russian river is described as flowing loosely through Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neva is the river that flows through St Petersburg into the Gulf of Finland.

clue.text: Energy and source of change bypassing a cricket team

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: to bypass something is to go round it and leave it out, so the a is dropped

parts.note: leaven, such as yeast, is what makes dough rise and transforms it

explanation.surface: Power and a catalyst for reform go round a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bypassing a' drops the A from LEAVEN, giving LEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields eleven players, so a team is commonly called an eleven.

clue.text: Remains with member of flock in religious retreat

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
a ram is a male sheep, one of a flock

explanation.surface: Ashes and a sheep from the flock are kept at a spiritual retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flock' suggests a congregation, fitting the religious picture, but here it means sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community where people withdraw for spiritual practice.

clue.text: Very short man of honour mostly receiving a lot of attention after being pushed over

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece sits inside the other
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the knight goes

parts.note: a knight holds an honour from the monarch

indicators.note: pushed over means knocked backwards, so the word is read in reverse
a lot of but not all, so the last letter of the word for attention is lost

parts.note: heed is attention, as in pay heed

explanation.surface: A tiny knight is the centre of attention after being knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' and 'mostly' each lop off a last letter; 'pushed over' then gives EEH, which 'receiving' sets inside KNIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-high describes something so small it reaches only to a person's knee, as in knee-high to a grasshopper.

clue.text: German writer attempts unfinished article

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is left off

parts.note: goes are attempts, as in have a few goes
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A German author tries but never finishes an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, author of Faust, is the most celebrated figure of German literature.

clue.text: Is avenged, providing information about Steve misbehaving

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the information word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting wrongly, so the letters of Steve are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone takes revenge after giving the lowdown on Steve's bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' scrambles the name to ETSEV, and 'about' wraps the slang for information round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get even with someone is the idiom for paying them back, taking revenge for a wrong.

clue.text: Film-maker left America after going round California

indicators.note: after means the America part comes after the letter for left
going round means encircling, so the America letters enclose the state's

parts.note: US is America
CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A director quit the States after touring California.
explanation.definitionFit: George Lucas is the director and producer who created Star Wars, a film-maker by profession.

clue.text: Capone, say, unusually wealthy? Completely

parts.note: Al Capone the gangster supplies the first name Al, the say showing it is just one example of an Al

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, signalling the letters of wealthy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was the gangster Capone extraordinarily rich? Totally.
explanation.definitionFit: All the way is an idiom for fully or without reservation, as in I'm with you all the way.

clue.text: Liberal legislator upset when wrapped in your old wool?

indicators.note: wrapped in means enclosed, so this piece goes inside the old word for your

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords, a law-making chamber

explanation.surface: A Liberal lawmaker is upset to be wrapped in an old-fashioned woollen garment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' turns the letters bottom to top, giving REEPL. The question mark flags that wool is only one example of such material.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-ply describes yarn of three twisted strands, a common grade of knitting wool.

clue.text: Skulk around Northern Italian city — it's not very colourful

indicators.note: around means enclosing, so the skulking word goes round the letter

parts.note: to mooch is to loiter or skulk about
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Someone lurks about a northern Italian city that looks rather drab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Italian city' looks like Milan or Turin, but 'Northern' is just N and the city is Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Monochrome means in a single colour or black and white, so lacking variety of colour.

clue.text: Numerical data about one working in transport centres

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the data word goes round the other letters

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, are numerical data
I is the Roman numeral one
on means working, as with a machine switched on

explanation.surface: Statistics on one person employed in the transport sector.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway and bus stations are where journeys begin and end, the hubs of a transport network.

clue.text: Majority rule's ending, e.g. in the riots

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of the word is taken
riots here means wild disorder, so the letters gathered before it are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: The end of a regime arrives, for instance, amid civil unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority' looks like a political majority, but it means the age of majority. 'riots' is the anagram signal, and 'e.g.' is taken letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Majority is the age at which a person legally becomes an adult, eighteen in Britain.

clue.text: Being this? Ergo endless conceit, sadly

definitions.text: Being this? Ergo endless conceit, sadly

indicators.note: sadly means in a sorry state, so the gathered letters are shuffled
endless means the last letter of the word ergo is dropped

explanation.surface: If you are self-centred, it follows that your vanity has no limit, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ERGO to ERG, and 'sadly' shuffles ERG + CONCEIT. The whole clue also describes the answer: being self-obsessed means unending vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Egocentric means self-centred, thinking only of oneself, which naturally goes with boundless vanity.

clue.text: Canadian writer at court finally exonerated

parts.note: to court is to woo, as a suitor does

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Canadian author in the dock is ultimately cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, fitting 'exonerated', but it is the verb meaning to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Atwood, author of The Handmaid's Tale, is one of Canada's best-known novelists.

clue.text: Cakes and small servings of ice-cream

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ice cream is often served in cones

explanation.surface: A tea-shop menu offers cakes and little portions of ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones are small British baked goods, eaten with jam and cream at teatime, a kind of plain cake.

clue.text: Town retailer finally brought in kitchen item

indicators.note: brought in means introduced inside, so the letter goes into the kitchen item

parts.note: a stockpot is a large pan for making stock

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A shop at last brings in a piece of kitchen equipment for the town.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockport is a large town south-east of Manchester in England.

clue.text: No opening for compassion — it keeps church irritated

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the letters for church go within the shortened word
no opening means the first letter is removed

parts.note: pity is compassion

explanation.surface: No compassion is shown when the church is kept in a state of annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No opening for' leaves ITY, which 'keeps' the church abbreviation inside; the word 'it' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy describes skin that is irritated and makes you want to scratch.

clue.text: Getting upset first — notice?

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting upset means being turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tops means the best, first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being upset comes before being noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it.

clue.text: Exclamation about core component of lunch being like rubber

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes round the middle letters

parts.note: boy! is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, all but the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the main ingredient of lunch being rubbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber is springy and rebounds, so something rubbery is bouncy.

clue.text: Setter's supporting person showing vulgarity

parts.note: the setter speaks as I, so setter's is I'm, I am
pro means in favour of, supporting
per. is the grammatical abbreviation for person

explanation.surface: The puzzle-maker backs someone who behaves crudely.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means unseemly or indecent, the quality of something coarse and in poor taste.

clue.text: Nobleman cut round square in the twilight

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shortened title encloses the letter
cut means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a duke is a nobleman of the highest rank

explanation.surface: An aristocrat walks round the town square at sunset.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the darker stage of twilight, the fading light just before night.

clue.text: Plane having no place going backwards? Ditch

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: to sit something is to place or set it down

explanation.surface: An aircraft with nowhere to land turns back and comes down in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going backwards' gives TISON. 'Ditch' suggests a plane ditching in the sea, but it is the definition, to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, as you ditch something unwanted.
